entry_state: The return-right example retains a refund liability and separate recovery asset, then distinguishes estimate revision, actual return and settlement. Its direct and indirect cash-flow calculations agree under the stated pretax scope. The next warranty example has introduced two distinct promises and an allocation of 90 to the product and 18 to service; its two-period statement consequences continue on the next page.
exit_state: Distinct service promises, approved modifications and control before transfer determine revenue timing and presentation; cash alone does not. The cost examples retain inventory layers, prior write-downs and component histories. The sample-production case has separated PPE cost 120, inventory cost 6 and period expenses 6, then sold the samples for 8; its closing balances and cash-flow consequences continue on page 125.
findings: The service warranty states a uniform performance assumption and reconciles both annual statements and cash flows; unknown progress is not silently treated as zero.

Prospective allocation to distinct remaining goods and a cumulative catch-up for an integrated obligation are distinguished with complete two-period examples. Approved rights and independently supported progress remain prerequisites.
Principal and agent examples share net cash and profit 20 but differ in revenue and intermediate accounting. Revenue classification does not itself establish cash-flow net presentation.

Cost histories preserve FIFO versus weighted-average consequences, write-down reversal limits and prospective estimate changes. The PPE case begins without completing its later consequences. No additional confirmed defect.
